column3: Description

The Social Impact measures the social value created by the product’s sustainability and circularity initiatives. It helps evaluate how these efforts translate to societal well-being and how viable the product is from a social aspect.
column4: To provide a single metric to evaluate the social effect of the product.

column3: Measures the social and ethical impacts of the product's procurement processes. Focuses on ensuring that sourcing practices align with ethical fair trade principles and promotes local contribution.
column4: To ensure procurement aligns with ethical standards and local socio-economic goals.

column3: Measures the share of the product's suppliers that hold a recognised ethical or fair-trade certification (certified ethical suppliers ÷ total suppliers). Higher means more of the supply chain is independently certified against ethical labour and sourcing standards.
column4: To reduce labor and human-rights risks across the supply chain.
column9: Share = Number of certified ethical suppliers / Number of total suppliers\n\n(Share - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).

column3: Measures the share of local sourcing suppliers from the overall suppliers.
column4: To support local economy, reduce transport, and improve local involvement.
column9: Share = Number of local suppliers / Number of total suppliers\n\n(Share - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).\nProduct-level local-supplier *count* share; GRI 204-1 and ISO 26000 frame local sourcing by procurement *spend*, not supplier count — count basis is the author's simplification. 'Local' = community, else same country (see S1-3).

column3: Number of suppliers for sourcing and procurement involved throughout the whole product's lifecycle.
Number of suppliers certified from ethical standard bodies such as the Global Organic Textile Standard (GOTS), Fairmined, Fair Trade USA, the Rainforest Alliance, etc.
Number of suppliers located in the community. If not possible, extends to the same country.

Aggregates the product's effect on customer well-being into one score by combining customer satisfaction (S21), product health & safety (S22), customer-service timeliness (S23) and customer-service satisfaction (S24). Reflects the overall customer experience and quality of life delivered by the product.
column4: To guide product design, support, and safety improvement.

column3: Measures the average customer satisfaction of the product. Reflects consumer's perception of quality, reliability, and overall value of products. Needs a robust, standardized framework and methodology i.e. CSAT, NPS, CES, SERVQUAL, etc.
column4: To monitor customer's product perception and guide product and service improvement.
column9: Avg = Customer Feedback Results / Number of Surveyee\n\n(Avg - Min) / (Max - Min)

column3: Measures product health & safety as one minus the customer-incident rate — i.e. 1 − (reported customer safety incidents (S2-4) ÷ number of customers (S2-3)). Higher means fewer product-use safety incidents per customer.
column4: To minimize harm and accident risk.
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).\nProduct-level safety-rate complement; adapts GRI 416-2 incident disclosure / ISO 26000 §6.7.4. Rate construction author-defined.

column3: Customer feedback results.
The total number of survey respondents in a given timeframe.
The total number of customers in a given timeframe.
Total customer safety incidents related to the use of the product.
Measures the response times of customer inquiries and compared with its target value.
column4: To reduce customer's wait times and improve service experience.
column9: Avg = Response Times / Number of Inquiries\n\n(Avg - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Author-defined service-responsiveness ratio; concept per ISO 26000 §6.7.6. Band must be inverted (faster = better).

column3: Measures average satisfaction with the customer-service response — the mean service-feedback rating across handled inquiries (service feedback results (S2-7) ÷ number of inquiries (S2-6)), normalized to a target band. Distinct from S21 (product satisfaction): S24 rates the support experience.
column4: To ensure high quality support and strengthen customer loyalty.
column9: Avg = Service Feedback Results / Number of Inquiries\n\n(Avg - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Service-satisfaction (support), distinct from S21 product-satisfaction; ISO 10004 grounds satisfaction measurement.

column3: The time taken to respond to customer inquiries and complaints.
The total number of customer-service inquiries and complaints received in a given timeframe; denominator of S23 (response-time average) and S24 (service-satisfaction average).
The feedback score or ratings for the response given to customers.

Aggregates the product's workforce-welfare performance into one score by combining employee satisfaction (S31), the local-employment rate (S32), employee health and safety (S33), and the social-economic contribution to the workforce (S34). Higher means better working conditions and stronger socio-economic benefits for the people who make the product.
column4: To monitor the social performance for workforce related issues.

column3: Measures average employee satisfaction with working on the product, from staff feedback surveys (e.g. CSAT/eNPS), normalized against a company target band.
column4: To improve retention, productivity, and product quality.
column9: Avg = Employee Feedback Results / Total Employee\n\n(Avg - Min) / (Max - Min)

column3: Measures the share of employees hired from local communities to support local economies.
column9: Rate = Number of local employee / Total employee\n\n(Rate - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).

column3: Measures the well-being of employees, particularly in the context of manufacturing and production environments.
column4: To reduce harm, accident risk, and absenteeism.
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).

column3: Aggregate result of employee satisfaction/engagement surveys (e.g. CSAT/eNPS), used as the numerator of S31.
The total amount of employee directly involved in the product.
The total local residents employed involved in the product.
Number of workplace safety incidents per employee, aimed at minimizing risks.

Aggregates the product's socio-economic contribution to its workforce into one score by combining wage adequacy vs local cost of living (S3-5/S3-6), employee remuneration level (S3-6), and job creation (S3-7) — each scored 0–1 against a company target — then weight-averaging them. Designed for internal cross-site comparison.
column4: To provide the product's role in fostering socio-economic growth and workers' welfare within its value chain.
column9: Weighted sum of each underlying metrics compared to a target value or comparable product / standard
column18: This KPI is intended for internal company comparison i.e. shoes manufactured in germany vs in vietnam

column3: Wage-adequacy against local cost of living, scored 0–1 by comparing average employee salary (S3-6) to the local cost of living and benchmarking against a company target (per PSILCA's salary/living-wage ratio).
column18: Self-normalized 0–1 wage-adequacy component of S34 (input unit € is the raw input unit); scored against a company target, not a living-wage denominator (open re-model question, out of scope this pass).

column3: Average employee salary scored 0–1 by comparison to a company wage-adequacy target (e.g. salary vs local cost of living / living wage, per PSILCA p.38). Higher means pay is more adequate relative to the local standard of living.
column18: Self-normalized 0–1 salary-adequacy component of S34 (input unit € is the raw input unit); GRI 201-1 grounds the absolute-salary figure, PSILCA the salary/living-wage normalization.

column3: Jobs created for the product, scored 0–1 against a company job-creation target. Based on GRI 401-1 new-hire count, normalized so a higher score means more jobs created relative to target.
column18: Self-normalized 0–1 job-creation component of S34 (input unit # is the raw input unit); GRI 401-1 grounds the new-hire count, normalized against a company target.
